newsitem.title: USA: COMEX COPPER ENDS WEAKER, BUT OFF LOWS.
newsitem.headline: COMEX COPPER ENDS WEAKER, BUT OFF LOWS.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker on light fund and local liquidation, although rebounded from the lows, bucking the trend of the other base metals, most of which fell sharply.
The active September contract hit three-week lows, before rallying, but analysts saw few reasons to be bullish.
The active September contract finished at 104.85 cents down, 0.35 cents from Monday, trading in a range of 103.60 to 105.60 cents a lb. The spot month fell 0.50 cents to 104.70 cents a lb.

"We've been making lower lows, which is not a good sign technically," said William O'Neill, senior futures strategist with Merrill Lynch. "But I should say that every time this market looks like it's ready to break down, it rallies."
Fundamentally, London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks increased another 3,900 tonnes to 254,300 tonnes, while the cash-to-three-month backwardation weakened slightly to $18/$20 from $18/$23 Monday.
"It's hard to get excited about this market fundamentally," he said. "We haven't seen the Asian demand that we thought we were going to. We're seeing higher stocks and narrowing spreads."

He also noted that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's commitment of traders report is currently showing a heavily long speculative position. "The market is looking vulnerable to a bout of liquidation," O'Neill said.

Some brokers are holding out for a possibility of a squeeze of the LME September date, which could juice the market. "There's a feeling in the market that whoever was squeezing the market in July took August off but will return in September," one New York commission house broker said.

In other news, drought conditions in Papua New Guinea have ground copper concentrate shipments at the Ok Tedi mine to a halt, although sources expect that it would take several weeks before the drought would impact refined copper supplies in Japan and Europe, where the concentrates are smelted.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
